notes: Dapenkeng (Dabenkeng, Tapenkeng) culture of Taiwan and the Fujian coast; the page gives the span 'between 4000 and 3000 BC' and the Prehistory of Taiwan page 'Between 4000 and 3000 BC'; infobox 'Geographical range: coastal'. Extent: 'quickly spread around the coast of the island, as well as the Penghu islands'; type site in Bali District, New Taipei City; Fengbitou's lowest layer (Kaohsiung) and Bajiacun (Tainan) in the southwest; Keqiutou on Haitan Island and Fuguodun and Jinguishan on Kinmen on the Fujian side; likely origin 'the coast of what is now Fujian'. The shape is Taiwan (with Penghu and Kinmen) plus a Fuzhou disc, a coarse placement of a coastal culture (confidence 2). End: 'Around 2500 BC' the culture 'developed into locally differentiated cultures throughout Taiwan' (the Fengbitou in Penghu and the central and southern west coast; the Niuchouzi '2,500 BC to 1,000 BC' around Tainan; the Yuanshan in the northeast; the Dahu in the southwest, on the Prehistory of Taiwan page); the pages date the Dapenkeng to 3000 and the successors to 2500, so the island is nobody's land 2999..2501 on the pages opened. None of the successors has a dossier. Austronesian expansion and Hemudu influence ('the influence of the Hemudu and Majiabang cultures') are the page's hypotheses, not drawn. The older Changbin culture (15,000 to 5,000 years ago, east coast) and the Eluanbi culture ('until 5,000 years ago') lie before and partly in the project's range but have no dossier. No area figure.
